title: I.21: Fugue in Bb major

groocock.chapter: 7 Group 2: Fugues for Three Voices, without Stretto

entries.notes: tonal (first and third notes); remains in tonic for all of bar 5, modulates with e-naturals of bar 6; with C1
follows immediately without episode, giving impression of a fourth voice; countersubjects below
starts as answer but continues with intervals of the subject (diagram "S(A)")
incomplete; modulates to IV instead of back to vi

episodes.material: 17-18 virtually a repeat of bars 15-16 a second higher with lower voices interchanged; 19-22 variant of the fourth bar of the subject with free inversion of its first bar
30-32 free interchange of bars 19-21 with added third part; 33-35 interchange of 30-32

countersubjects.notes: I.21 is not in either interchange list on p.13. C1 same from its second bar on; its first bar unaltered with answers at bars 13 and 41, modified with subject (bar 9), combined shapes at 22, completely different at 26 and 37. C2 not a free part; same form at 13 and 26 in upper voices, altered when in the bass (22, 35, 37, 41); diagram marks it CII(inv) in the bass at 35 and 41

subject.answer: tonal (first and third notes answered tonally)
subject.notes: subject starts on the dominant and has the dominant as third note

key_plan: Group 2 table: Exp I V I | V | Dev EP vi ii EP IV IV | Final I

claims.claim: Of 48 bars, 34 are occupied by subject or answer together with the two countersubjects (greatest economy of material).
Simple exposition (no codetta/episode); redundant answer at bar 13.
Bass entry at 26 begins as answer but modulates vi-ii by continuing with subject intervals; answer at 35 modulates to IV instead of vi.
Coda (45-48) repeats bars 43-44 with interchange of outer voices.
